newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope in "great shape" two days after surgery.
newsitem.headline: Pope in "great shape" two days after surgery.

text.p: Pope John Paul was in "really great shape" on Thursday, two days after surgery to remove his appendix and officials said he planned to celebrate a public mass at the Vatican before the end of the month.
"He's in really great shape...smiling," Professor Attilio Maseri, the Pope's cardiologist, told Reuters after visiting the 76-year-old Pontiff with other doctors on Thursday morning.

"I'm really visiting him more for reasons of affection and devotion at this point than for medical reasons," he said. "His heart is behaving splendidly. I would be out of a job as a cardiologist if I had to be here because he has problems."

The Polish-born Pope had a 50-minute operation at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday to remove an inflamed appendix. Doctors said biopsies showed that there was no trace of any recurrence of a colon tumour removed in 1992.
"Everybody is happy with the whole event and he's the first one to be happy," Maseri said in an interview.
Other doctors said all the Pope's vital signs were fine and that he might begin taking solid food later on Thursday if his digestive processes returned to normal.
Doctors did not release an official medical bulletin on Thursday. The next is expected for Friday at 1000 GMT.
Louis Nigro, the charge d'affaires of the U.S embassy to the Vatican, visited the Gemelli to convey President Bill Clinton's regards and was told by Vatican officials that all was proceeding well.

"President Bill Clinton and (U.S. Ambassador to the Vatican) Raymond Flynn asked me to convey to the Holy Father the hopes and prayers of the American people and best wishes for a speedy recovery," Nigro told Reuters.
Nigro said Vatican officials had told him that the Pope had made plans to celebrate a public mass at the Vatican on October 27 to celebrate a religious anniversary.
Papal masses usually last some three hours.
Vatican sources, however, said the Pope would probably resume short audiences even before October 27.
The Pope is keen to be in good form by November 1, when he will mark the 50th anniversary of his ordination as a priest. He has invited all priests also ordained in 1946 to come to Rome.
The sources said the Pope, who is taking strolls in the corridors of his high-security 10th floor suite, was impatient to leave the hospital
"It's not for me to decide but I think he might get out early. He is so energetic. I'm sure he is very anxious to go," Maseri said.

Professor Francesco Crucitti, the chief surgeon who operated on the Pope, said after the surgery that the Pope would stay in hospital for about seven days but could leave earlier if there were no complications.

Doctors who have treated the Pope for the appendix have declined to discuss explicitly another problem that has been ailing the Pontiff -- a sometimes violently trembling left hand, rigidity of the facial muscles, and a slow stooped gait.
Outside observers say this may be a symptom of Parkinson's disease or a related neurological disorder.
Although doctors have suggested to the Pope that he slow down, the Pontiff has four trips planned for next year, including a visit to his native Poland.
